exposure: Ultrasound-guided Erector Spinae Plane (ESP) block with 0.2% ropivacaine and nalbuphine
Ultrasound-guided Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block with 0.2% ropivacaine and nalbuphine
outcome: Total administration of rescue analgesia within 24 hours
cohort: Sixty pregnant women (age > 18 years) scheduled for elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Erector Spinae Plane (ESP) block provided a significantly prolonged duration of analgesia and a reduction in the total administration of rescue analgesia within 24 hours compared to Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block.
mod_finding: ESP block provided superior postoperative analgesia compared to TAP block in women undergoing caesarean section.
